Show what a rule would match and do, acting on nothing

## Usage

```text
chainmail rule dry-run (<id|name> | -f FILE) [--trigger new|schedule|manual] [--account NAME] [flags]
```

## Examples

```sh
chainmail rule dry-run receipts
# an unsaved rule, against the newest cached mail
chainmail rule dry-run -f receipts.toml --trigger new
```

## Flags

```text
      --account string   only this account (default: every account the rule covers)
  -f, --file string      dry-run the unsaved rule in this rule file
      --trigger string   new: the newest 200 cached messages per account; schedule or manual: the whole cache (default manual)
```

## Global flags

```text
      --output string   output format: json or table (default $CHAINMAIL_OUTPUT, then cli.toml, then table on a terminal, json otherwise)
      --socket string   daemon socket (default $CHAINMAIL_SOCKET, then cli.toml, then /run/chainmail/chainmail.sock)
```
